title: Suffixes
subtitle: -er, -or, -ful, -less, -ly, -ness, -y
summary: Use common suffixes like -er, -ful, -less and -ness to understand and build new words.

lesson.heading: What is a suffix?
lesson.text: A **suffix** comes at the end of a word. It often changes the word from one kind of word to another - from a verb to a noun, or from an adjective to an adverb.

lesson.heading: Common suffixes
rows: makes an adverb from an adjective
makes an abstract noun from an adjective
makes an adjective from a noun

lesson.heading: -er and -or: people
lesson.text: We add **-er** or **-or** to a verb to make the person who does it. A **worker** works, a **swimmer** swims, a **builder** builds.

examples.text: He's a hard **worker**. He works 12 hours a day.
She's a very good **swimmer**. She was in the Olympic team.
Her tennis is much better now that she has a new **instructor**.
A **footballer** is a person who plays football.

lesson.heading: -er and -or: machines and things
lesson.text: The same two suffixes also make the name of a machine or a thing that does the job.

examples.text: We've got a new gas **cooker**, so the food should be delicious!
Can we use our **calculators** in the maths test?
A tin **opener** is a thing for opening tins.
A hair **dryer** is a thing you use to dry your hair.

left.label: -ful = full of
left.text: The thing has a lot of it.
examples: Thanks for the information. It was very **useful**.
What a **beautiful** photo. I think it will win the competition.

right.label: -less = without
right.text: The thing has none of it.
examples: This book is no help at all - it's **useless**.
I can't finish this book - it's **endless**.
If something is **painless**, it doesn't hurt.

lesson.heading: -ly and -ness
lesson.text: **-ly** turns an adjective into an adverb (how you do something). **-ness** turns an adjective into a noun for the feeling or quality.

examples.text: He was late for work, so he went **quickly** to the station.
They are **happily** married with two young children.
The mother was smiling with **happiness** as she held her baby.
Thank you very much for all your **kindness**.

lesson.heading: -y: from noun to adjective
lesson.text: Add **-y** to a noun and you get an adjective, often about the weather or what something is made of.

examples.text: That beach is very popular with tourists because it is long and **sandy**.
It's a lovely **sunny** day - let's go to the beach.
It was wet and **windy** most of last week.

lesson.text: Some words change their spelling before the suffix: *happy* becomes *happily* and *happiness*; *easy* becomes *easily*.

exercises.prompt: It's a lovely ___ day - let's go to the beach.
exercises.explanation: -y makes an adjective from a noun: sun - sunny.

exercises.prompt: Her tennis is much better now that she has a new ___.
exercises.hint: (a person who teaches you a sport)
exercises.explanation: -or makes the person who does the job.

exercises.prompt: They are ___ married with two young children.
exercises.explanation: -ly makes an adverb from an adjective; happy becomes happily.

exercises.prompt: Thanks for the information. It was very ___.
exercises.explanation: -ful means 'full of', so useful means 'full of use'.

exercises.prompt: Match each adjective with the noun it goes with.
I'm tired because I slept very ___ last night.
exercises.explanation: -ly makes the adverb: bad becomes badly.

exercises.prompt: The waiter was very ___ and explained everything on the menu.
exercises.explanation: -ful means 'full of', so helpful means 'full of help'.

exercises.prompt: Thank you very much for all your ___.
exercises.explanation: -ness makes a noun from an adjective: kind becomes kindness.

exercises.prompt: It's important not to make ___ mistakes in your writing.
Do you know a good ___ who could do some work on our house?
exercises.explanation: -er makes the person who does the job: build becomes builder.

exercises.prompt: Does each -er / -or word mean a person or a thing?

exercises.statement: If something is painless, it hurts a lot.
exercises.explanation: If something is painless, it does not hurt. -less means 'without'.

exercises.prompt: Describe the beach the tourists love.
exercises.answer: That beach is long and sandy.
